entries.title: Drowning deaths soar in France as Europe buckles in peak of heatwave
entries.snippet: Forty people have drowned in heatwave-related deaths in France since last Thursday, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu says.

entries.title: UN says it will evacuate sailors stranded in Strait of Hormuz, as Rubio warns against tolls
entries.snippet: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned Iran that no country can charge fees for ships to travel through the strait.

entries.title: Israeli troops kill two in south Lebanon after lull in fighting, authorities say
entries.snippet: Israel's military says the two men were Hezbollah operatives, but the Iran-backed group accuses it of a ceasefire violation.

entries.title: Germany rail network briefly halted nationwide due to IT malfunction
entries.snippet: Rail company Deutsche Bahn had to pause train services across the country for more than two-and-a-half hours.

entries.title: Dozens of ships head through Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran deal
entries.snippet: Traffic in the waterway has risen since the US and Iran signed a deal aimed at ending the war, including 42 ships on Saturday alone.

entries.title: UN commission of inquiry says Israel committing genocide in Gaza by deliberately targeting children
entries.snippet: Israel rejects the new report by the three-member expert panel, calling it a "libellous sham".

entries.title: Eight sentenced to 450 years in prison over anti-ICE riot where officer was shot
entries.snippet: An officer was shot in the neck during the Texas disorder by "Antifa Cell operatives", prosecutors said.

entries.title: Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba sues US government over defence blacklist
entries.snippet: It is suing the US defence department after it was added to a list of firms with ties to the Chinese military.

entries.title: Zambia ex-president's family wins latest legal battle over what should happen to his body
entries.snippet: Edgar Lungu's family and the Zambian government remained in dispute 12 months after he died.

entries.title: Spider which uses spring trap to capture prey discovered in Australia
entries.snippet: Researchers say their hunting method - which allows them to prey on dangerous ants - is unprecedented.

entries.title: US top court says Rastafarian man cannot sue prison guards who cut his dreadlocks
entries.snippet: The former Louisiana inmate argued his Rastafarian faith was violated after prison officials focibly shaved off his hair.

entries.title: Irish government to contribute £197m to cross-border rail services
entries.snippet: The money will come from the last allocation from the Irish government's Shared Island Fund.

entries.title: Trump anticipates better relationship with Colombia under new leader
entries.snippet: Abelardo de la Espriella, who preliminary results suggest is Colombia's next president, had Trump's endorsement.

entries.title: Montreal shooting leaves officer, civilian and suspect dead
entries.snippet: It was the first time in 24 years that a Montreal police officer was killed in the line of duty, the city's police chief said.

entries.title: Ransom note claims Nancy Guthrie died after abduction
entries.snippet: On Tuesday, Today show presenter Savannah Guthrie begged anyone with information to come forward, saying, "We are in agony."

entries.title: Iran says no new commitments on nuclear sites after Vance says inspectors to be invited back
entries.snippet: Iran's foreign ministry says it made "no new commitments" on nuclear inspections after talks in Switzerland.

entries.title: Dettol apologises after ad to clean up 'toxic men' backfires in China
entries.snippet: The ad sparked accusations of sexism in China, after featuring a man looking for a partner who is "not tainted by other men".

entries.title: Inquiry ordered after building fire kills 15 in north India city
entries.snippet: Witnesses described people jumping from windows to escape, while rescue teams broke through a wall to save lives.

entries.title: Myanmar army killed over 700 civilians in six months, UN says
entries.snippet: The new UN report says the 702 civilian deaths over six months last year included 153 children.

entries.title: Russian troop build-up threatens city seen as key to seizing Ukraine's Donbas
entries.snippet: If Kostyantynivka falls, Russian forces would be able push towards Ukraine's last remaining strongholds in the east.

entries.title: Supreme Court rules that prison guards can't be sued for shaving Rastafarian's head
entries.snippet: The Supreme Court ruled that a Louisiana prisoner whose dreadlocks were forcibly shaved off by prison guards cannot sue the guards under a federal law to protect the religious rights of prisoners.

entries.title: In symbolic vote, Congress directs Trump to remove forces from Iran war
entries.snippet: The measure to remove U.S. armed forces from hostilities with Iran does not require the president's signature, nor does it carry the force of law. But it reflects bipartisan frustration with the war.

entries.title: Congress passes the largest housing affordability bill in decades
entries.snippet: An expansive bipartisan bill intended to bring down the cost of housing by boosting the supply of homes has passed both houses of Congress, and is headed to the president's desk for a signature.

entries.title: Is AI 'one big bubble'? Behind the tech sell-off
entries.snippet: Investors are selling off AI-related stocks as doubts are starting to surface over whether the massive spending on AI is worth the investment and whether it's "one big bubble."

entries.title: Portugal's Ronaldo shakes off World Cup doubters, scores 2 after sluggish start
entries.snippet: At 41, Cristiano Ronaldo is one of the oldest players in the World Cup. Against the Democratic Republic of Congo he was mostly invisible and questions mounted. Against Uzbekistan, he sparkled.

entries.title: A Revolutionary War soldier's DNA links him to living relatives
entries.snippet: Continental Army soldier John Pumphrey enlisted as a teenager in 1777 and fought at significant battles before his death in action against the British in Camden, S.C.

entries.title: Afghan Taliban hold first, closed-door talks with EU on deportations
entries.snippet: Rights groups criticized the meeting, saying it undermines the EU's human rights obligations.

entries.title: U.S. lifts Iran oil sanctions. And, federal judge rules SAVE voter tool unlawful
entries.snippet: The U.S. has temporarily lifted oil sanctions on Iran as peace talks continue. And, a federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's data system, known as SAVE, is unlawful.

entries.title: Who would pay for Trump's proposed $300 billion Iran reconstruction fund?
entries.snippet: It's still unclear who would fund a proposed $300 billion reconstruction plan for Iran. Former National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan called the whole approach "something entirely new."

entries.title: When falling housing prices are good news — and when they're not
entries.snippet: Denver renters are celebrating falling housing costs. But sometimes cheaper housing is a sign of economic decline. How can you tell the difference?

entries.title: Maryland Democrats pick their U.S. House nominees as Moore wins primary for governor
entries.snippet: Rising party star Gov. Wes Moore won the Democratic primary in his bid for reelection to a second term. Republican voters hope to return the state to GOP leadership by picking a candidate they think can unseat him.

entries.title: Wilson wins GOP nomination for South Carolina governor after Trump hedges his bet on race
entries.snippet: South Carolina Attorney General Alan Wilson won a runoff election on Tuesday, swiftly routing the candidate initially endorsed by President Donald Trump to be the Republican nominee for governor.

entries.title: Trains across Germany halted for hours by communication system outage
entries.snippet: The main national railway operator, Deutsche Bahn, said shortly before 1 a.m. — nearly 2 1/2 hours after it first reported the outage — that the problem had been resolved and service was resuming "step by step."

entries.title: NCAA panel approves new eligibility rules giving Division I athletes 5 years to play 5 seasons

entries.title: Federal judge dismisses Justice Department lawsuit seeking detailed Maryland voter data
entries.snippet: The Trump administration's attempts to obtain state-level voter data have suffered yet another legal blow.

entries.snippet: Iran and the U.S. are once again at odds, this time over nuclear inspections. The U.S. said that the UN nuclear watchdog will inspect Iran's facilities, but Iran says no deal is in place. It was just one of several disagreements since the weekend meetings in Switzerland between t

entries.title: In rare rebuke, Senate votes to limit Trump's war powers in Iran
entries.snippet: Congress never authorized military action in Iran, but the U.S. Senate today voted to limit President Trump's Iran war powers in a rare rebuke. White House correspondent Liz Landers caught up with Senators on both sides of the aisle.

entries.title: Ex-Energy Secretary Moniz breaks down challenges of nuclear negotiations with Iran
entries.snippet: To discuss the U.S. nuclear negotiations with Iran, Amna Nawaz spoke with Ernest Moniz. Trained as a nuclear physicist, he was the Energy Secretary during the Obama administration and was a chief architect and the lead technical negotiator of the 2015 Iran nuclear agreement. He's

entries.title: Federal appeals court allows Trump to resume expanded use of speedy deportations
entries.snippet: The ruling was a big victory for the Republican administration, which views the expansion of so-called expedited removal as a key tool for carrying out its mass deportation policy.

entries.title: News Wrap: Supreme Court sides with Trump administration
entries.snippet: In our news wrap Tuesday, the Supreme Court sided with the Trump administration in an immigration case strengthening the government's power to deport green card holders accused of crimes and the Justice Department has reportedly withdrawn grand jury subpoenas to reporters at The

entries.title: A decade after Brexit, UK voters reflect on decision to break from European Union
entries.snippet: Tuesday marks the 10th anniversary of the most divisive day in Britain's recent history: Brexit, the vote to leave the European Union. Voters were promised a Britain free of European laws, decreased immigration, and a major boost to business, without the EU's economic constraints

entries.title: How the federal student loan changes could impact borrowers
entries.snippet: Federal student loans will undergo significant changes starting July 1. These changes will not only restructure the loan system, but also the repayment options for millions of borrowers. Some might see higher monthly payments, others will have to deal with stricter caps on how mu

entries.title: Farmers struggle with crops as climate change makes weather less predictable
entries.snippet: More than half of the continental U.S. is facing drought conditions. But other parts of the country are facing the opposite problem. Extreme weather conditions can have major impacts on farmers and their crops at a time when they're already facing high production costs. Paul Solm

entries.title: 'The Queer Face of War' chronicles hardships for Ukraine's LGBTQ+ community during war
entries.snippet: It's been more than four years since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. While war has impacted the lives of nearly all Ukrainians, life has been especially challenging for members of the LGBTQ+ community. Author and photojournalist J. Lester Feder's book chronicles

entries.title: Read the House transcripts of Bill Gates and Lesley Groff's interviews in Epstein probe
entries.snippet: The House Oversight Committee on Tuesday released transcripts of the testimonies by Bill Gates and Lesley Groff in closed-door depositions before the panel in June as part of its investigation into the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

entries.title: The reflecting pool is about to be drained, again. Here's what to know
entries.snippet: Green water, floating liner chunks, and workers dumping jugs of hydrogen peroxide. These are the images that have characterized the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in the weeks since its reopening following President Donald Trump's ordered renovations.

entries.title: UN adopts resolution to ensure perpetrators of crimes against peacekeepers face justice
entries.snippet: Nearly 1,100 peacekeepers from countries around the world have lost their lives in the line of duty and thousands of others have been injured since 1948, according to U.N. peacekeeping department figures.

entries.title: U.S. and Iran disagree over whether Tehran has agreed to nuclear inspections
entries.snippet: The U.S. and Iran were in dispute Tuesday over whether Tehran had agreed to allow U.N. inspections of its nuclear sites.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump says nuclear inspectors will be able to enter Iran at 'appropriate time'
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump insisted Tuesday that Iran agreed to United Nations watchdog inspections of its nuclear sites, but said there is "no rush."

entries.title: U.S. eases restriction on Iran's World Cup team, allowing travel 2 days before next match
entries.snippet: Iran's squad has complained about the travel restrictions levied on the team.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Ebola in DR Congo sees record first-month caseload
entries.snippet: The UN says the DR Congo has reported 1,000 Ebola cases, the most ever in the first month of any Ebola outbreak in Africa. Meanwhile, Kenya's health minister says he is halting a US-backed Ebola quarantine center.

entries.title: Lebanon's lose-lose: Is there another way out of conflict?
entries.snippet: The new US-Iran peace deal seems to be forcing Lebanon to choose between Israel's sphere of influence or Iran's. It wants neither. But could there be a better alternative, achieved with the help of regional diplomacy?

entries.title: Curacao's trailblazing doctor at the World Cup
entries.snippet: Suzanne Huurman is the only female chief doctor at the 2026 World Cup. Her work is inspiring change in men's football.

entries.title: Poland, Ukraine: Dispute between two close allies deepens
entries.snippet: Polish President Karol Nawrocki last week stripped Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Poland's highest state honor. How did it come to this? And what has it got to do with next year's election in Poland?

entries.title: Scotland: Sturgeon's ex-husband Peter Murrell jailed for 5 years and 3 months
entries.snippet: Peter Murrell pleaded guilty to embezzling funds in his role as chief executive of the Scottish National Party. He held the SNP's purse strings while his then-wife, Nicola Sturgeon, was Scottish First Minister.

entries.title: US, Iran give conflicting claims over Hormuz fees
entries.snippet: US top diplomat Rubio said Washington will not accept tolls on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. But Iran has said they want to charge "maritime service fees." And Israel and Lebanon are set for talks in the US.

entries.title: Colombia: The 'Tiger's' victory signals a rightward shift
entries.snippet: With the election of Abelardo de la Espriella, an ultra-right-wing outsider has won the presidential runoff in Colombia for the first time. The tight victory marks a political shift and could trigger new conflicts.

entries.title: Ukraine says major Crimea bridge destroyed in latest attack
entries.snippet: Ukraine continues to hit infrastructure on the Crimea to isolate the Russian-annexed peninsula. Meanwhile, Russia attacked Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown with a ballistic missile in a deadly strike.

entries.title: Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher Jimmy Lai honored by DW
entries.snippet: Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."

entries.title: Experts fired by Trump resurrect mothballed climate website
entries.snippet: Fired US federal workers have revived a defunct climate website — pushing back as the Trump administration escalates cuts to publicly funded science and research.

entries.title: India: What’s driving the intense pressure on students?
entries.snippet: The reported deaths of aspiring medical students in India have exposed the immense pressures of the country's high-stakes examination system and a worsening mental-health crisis.

entries.title: Afghan Taliban clamp down on women, smartphones, protests
entries.snippet: The Taliban are tightening the screws on women's clothing, shooting at protesters and ordering even their own officials to stop using smartphones. Behind the regime's omnipresent control, there are signs of deep anxiety.

entries.title: Wanted: Jobs, critical minerals as Zambia's election nears
entries.snippet: Zambians head to the polls in August with jobs and living costs at the top of their concerns. The outcome could also impact the ongoing global competition for critical minerals and redefine ties with China and the US.

entries.title: Schweinsteiger's Ivory Coast comments spark racism debate
entries.snippet: Bastian Schweinsteiger's TV analysis of Germany's World Cup opponents Ivory Coast appeared to draw on racist stereotypes. For some observers, the comments are evidence that racist tropes are still common in football.

entries.title: Europe heat wave: France measures hottest-ever day
entries.snippet: Monuments in Paris are working on reduced hours, and dozens of people in France have drowned during the heat wave. Britain, France, Italy and Spain have issued red alerts and health warnings. More on DW.

entries.title: Turkey arrests more than 200 in crackdown before NATO summit
entries.snippet: The Ankara prosecutor's office said 209 people were detained, while 32 others remained at large. Turkey has announced a ban on demonstrations amid preparations for next month's NATO summit in the capital.

entries.title: Europe is spending billions to rearm, so why the delays?
entries.snippet: European countries have been trying to scale up their military capabilities, but their current defense production and procurement model is not fit for purpose, say experts.

entries.title: EU hosts Taliban for migrant return talks in Brussels
entries.snippet: The EU is hosting Taliban officials after Belgium granted temporary visas for talks on returning failed Afghan asylum-seekers. The meeting is one of the bloc's highest-level contacts with the Taliban since 2021.

entries.title: Germany news: Merz hails pension reform proposals
entries.snippet: Chancellor Merz says a proposed pension reform package should be fully implemented. A survey has shown that almost half of teachers in Germany find pupils' behavior stressful.
